A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BridgeEQA benchmark and EMVR method, with readable text, figures, tables, and mathematics. v1 ends after its references despite mentioning appendix details; v2 supplies Supplementary Sections A–E. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five EQA configurations across three VLMs, dataset-quality measurements, and human alignment of Image Citation Relevance.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and additionally reports open-source model evaluations and condition-rating performance stratified by scene-graph size.

M1.justification: The scene-graph construction and EMVR state, observation, policy, and MOVE/COMPARE/REASON/RESPOND actions remain unchanged. The new Inspection EQA framing and clarification that graph construction requires no GPS or external sensors do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 200 Vermont bridges, 9,586 images, and 2,200 QA pairs. The supplementary evaluations use subsets of this coverage. Dams, tunnels, and pipelines are proposed applications, not newly evaluated domains.

E2.justification: The matched main experiments retain Multi-Frame VLM, Socratic LLM with scene graphs, and Multi-Frame VLM with scene graphs as baselines. Appendix E applies existing methods to additional model backbones; it introduces no new baseline algorithm or comparator replacement in the retained experiments.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds restricted evaluations with Qwen3-VL 8B-Thinking, Qwen3-VL 30B-A3B, and Nemotron-3 Nano-30B-A3B, using three configurations because of context limits. Tables 3–4 specify scenes with fewer than 30 images, although their footnotes single out the 8B model and exact sample counts are unspecified. The main 1,100-QA protocol and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D and Figures 14–15 systematically break down condition-rating accuracy by node and edge counts across all five configurations and three proprietary models. This substantially extends the analysis of graph-size sensitivity beyond v1's aggregate comparisons and qualitative failure examples. These are observational breakdowns, not controlled graph ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both report three annotators, averaged human judgments, and Spearman correlation of 0.817. Appendix A supplies sampling and scoring details without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 11 are unchanged, but Tables 3–4 add open-source results and Figures 14–15 add graph-size breakdowns. For example, Qwen3-VL 30B-A3B with EMVR scene-graph-only reports 29.3% exact-match and 76.8% within-1 accuracy. These are newly reported restricted-setting results, not improvements over v1 scores. The separate claim of 100% accuracy in a 100-QA human audit is removed.

T1.justification: The graph definition and mathematical MDP formulation are retained. Section 3.1 introduces a conceptual Inspection EQA checklist, but no new mathematical assumptions, propositions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 motivates infrastructure inspection as an EQA domain; v2 explicitly claims Inspection EQA as a general problem class in the abstract and contributions, with criteria in Section 3.1. This extends the framing while retaining the benchmark, metric, EMVR, and numerical performance claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes graph-size trends to context length and claims EMVR suffers less degradation. It expands open-model limitations to context capacity, hallucinated calls, and action loops, while removing the computational-cost and future-experiment discussion. Section 4.4 also replaces cross-component 'Integrative' reasoning with 'Aggregative' overall-condition reasoning, retaining the reported percentage.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C substantially expand documentation: the 100-sample citation-perturbation study, five-point human ratings, removal of the first two report pages, 200-by-200-pixel filtering, parsing-failure handling, and QA validation. These disclose existing procedures rather than demonstrate pipeline changes. v2 adds a project access URL but removes the estimated 2.2-billion-token computation cost.

R1.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-VL, Nemotron 3, Gemini 2.5, BridgeElSpect, and From Pixels to Rating references, while removing Chen et al.'s bridge-inspection VLM paper. Section 2.2 revises the research gap from predominantly single-image processing to the absence of a complete inspection reasoning chain. Most related-work positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, limitations, and conclusion receive focused edits. v2 adds the Inspection EQA subsection and organized Supplementary Sections A–E, with corresponding renumbering. Much of the main methodology, dataset description, and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is substantially redrawn to show context accumulation and all four actions. Figure 8 changes counts to equivalent percentages, and Figure 9 changes its category label. v2 adds dataset/source-report examples, two graph-size heatmaps, and two results tables; several retained figures are resized or relocated and captions shortened.

improvement.justification: Appendices A and C supply validation and preprocessing details that v1 referenced without including, improving transparency. Appendices D and E add useful diagnostic and open-model evidence. The gain is limited by incompletely specified evaluation subsets and observational analyses that do not establish the proposed causal explanation. Removing the quantified human QA audit and computation-cost disclosure partially offsets these benefits.
